name: Nadi Aur Pahar
competency: One-to-one correspondence, progressive ordinal counting, and spatial path traversal on stepping stone river crossings
ncertStandard: Grade 1 & 2 Mathematics: Joyful Mathematics Chapter 2 (Counting & Traditional Games)
overview: Inspired by the classic Indian childhood schoolyard game 'Nadi Aur Pahar' (River and Mountain), children cross a rushing river by hopping only on sturdy white mountain stones (Pahar). When hopped on, each stone reveals its sequential number and counts aloud (1, 2, 3...) until reaching the safe riverbank.
learningOutcomes: Develop 1-to-1 correspondence through tactile hopping interactions
Discover sequential numbers dynamically upon hopping rather than pre-printed clues
Reinforce number pronunciation and verbal counting with browser speech synthesis
Learn spatial path planning by distinguishing safe mountain stones (Pahar) from river rapids (Nadi)
